Zakharivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakharivka, Ukraine

Not demolished. Existing by 1851 per tombstone dating, this cemetery is marked as Jewish on a 1941 Russian topographic map; most tombstones from the older section were apparently removed, likely for construction, though a postwar section remained in use until 1982. Population reached 1,732 (48%) by 1897, with most local Jews engaged in agriculture; a 1920s Jewish colony, later named Frunzovka (1927), included 25 families from Rashkiv alongside local families, supporting a Jewish elementary school. Population reached 520 by 1939. Nazi occupation from August 3, 1941 murdered 56 Jews on October 4, 1941; all 97 people known to have been executed in Zakharivka during WWII are presumed Jewish. Tombstone inscriptions confirm Jewish presence continued at least into the 1980s.
